Accessibility and learning help

Read without an account, use the keyboard, choose a print copy or keep an offline reader. The general textbook needs no drone, VR headset or network pod.

Move around a long page

  • Press Tab to move between controls and Enter to activate a link or button. Use Space or Enter to expand an answer.
  • The first skip link moves to the main content. On chapter pages it keeps your selected chapter.
  • Back to top appears after scrolling. It returns to the page heading and moves keyboard focus there.
  • On a small screen, expand Course navigation to find chapters and tools. The menu identifies the current unit and chapter, closes after a selection, and closes with Escape. On desktop, the current chapter is highlighted in its expanded unit. Wide code, tables and diagrams can scroll within their own region.

Work through a manageable lesson

Choose an allocated lesson route for a focused reading, example, activity, specific feedback and later retry. Chapter pathways cover a broader topic; they are not instructions to complete a whole chapter in one lesson.

Read, print or keep a copy

Use your browser’s zoom controls to enlarge text. Chapter pages offer Print student copy and Print with answers. Download a self-contained unit reader or the complete library before disconnecting. Unit readers include their diagrams; full-size diagram links and text descriptions support online reading.

Checks and their limits

Publication runs browser checks in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, including automated accessibility scans. See the release checks and downloadable reports. Automated scans do not establish full accessibility conformance.

Independent screen-reader review, real-device zoom checks, visual diagram review and classroom trials remain ongoing. We do not claim complete WCAG compliance. Read the acceptance checklist and pending human checks.

Report a barrier

Report an accessibility or learning problem on GitHub. Include the page address, what you tried, your browser/device and the barrier. Avoid posting student names or work. If you cannot use GitHub, ask your teacher to record the issue and provide an alternative format while it is investigated.
